device.name: ThermoPro TempSpike / TP9xx BBQ Thermometer
device.notes:
Extracted from com.thermopro.thermopro v1.21 (87MB, TempPro APKPure XAPK).
Decompiled: 14,930 classes. Package: cn.com.adsmart.wifibbq.
ThermoPro uses BLE Mesh (not simple BLE GATT) for multi-probe BBQ thermometers.
Adsmart is the OEM behind ThermoPro's connected devices.
BLE Mesh GATT Proxy: The phone connects as a GATT proxy to the mesh network.
Mesh operations: opcodes, TTL, IV index, sequence numbers, publish intervals,
segmented messages, source/destination addressing.
Three distinct device change-utility families identified in the code:
TP9012, TP940 (4-probe BBQ), TP980 (advanced with history and IEEE 754 float encoding).

issued_to_client: Nothing — the provisioner issues the keys rather than receiving them
credentials.notes: No WiFi passphrase is involved; the thermometer is BLE Mesh only, despite the `cn.com.adsmart.wifibbq` package name. The mesh keys are the credentials that matter: without the NetKey a client cannot decrypt the node's messages, which is why replacing the app means either re-provisioning or recovering the keys from it.
stored_on_device: Application key (AppKey) bound to the node's models

factory_reset.effect: A reset to the unprovisioned state is required before a new provisioner can take the node, and it clears the node's address and keys. BLE Mesh defines this as a Node Reset message, but the button sequence that triggers it locally differs across the TP9012, TP940 and TP980 families and was not established from the app. Consult the model's manual rather than guessing.

methods.description: Provision the thermometer as a BLE Mesh node over the PB-GATT bearer, then talk to it through the GATT Proxy using the resulting network and application keys.

steps.action: Power the thermometer on. If it was previously provisioned, reset it to the unprovisioned state first — it will otherwise ignore a new provisioner.
Scan for unprovisioned device beacons, matching local name prefix TP, TempPro, BBQ or iBBQ.
Connect over the PB-GATT provisioning bearer.
Run the BLE Mesh provisioning exchange, assigning the node a unicast address and issuing the network key.
Bind an application key to the node's models so its temperature messages can be decrypted.
steps.expect: The node publishes temperature messages to the configured destination address.

steps.action: Reconnect through the GATT Proxy service for ongoing reads; provisioning itself uses a different bearer.

setup.notes:
This one is not a plain GATT device: it is a BLE Mesh node, so it must be provisioned before it will answer anything. The phone acts as the mesh provisioner, and provisioning is what assigns the node its unicast address and gives it the network and application keys. Until that happens the thermometer only emits unprovisioned device beacons.
The practical consequence for a replacement client: you cannot simply connect and read, the way you can with the BLE sensors elsewhere in this repo. You need a mesh stack, and you need the network key — which means either provisioning the node yourself (removing it from the vendor app's network) or extracting the keys from the app's own store.
Confidence is medium: BLE Mesh provisioning is a published standard and the app's use of it is clear from the decompiled code, but the exchange has not been run against a device here.

rejoin.notes: Moving the thermometer to a different mesh network means re-provisioning it, which requires resetting it to the unprovisioned state first — a node can belong to one network at a time. A client that already holds the network key rejoins the existing network without any reset.

command_opcodes.description: Temperature and battery status upload. Bytes [2,3] = probe 1 temp, [4,5] = probe 2 temp
command_opcodes.name: TEMP_AND_BATTERY_UPLOAD

device_families.temperature_encoding_detail: (byteHigh * 256 + byteLow) / 10.0 °C — getProTemp() from two separate bytes

device_families.description: Advanced 4-probe BBQ thermometer with meat temperature settings
device_families.protocol_notes:
Multi-request flow for reading all probes. Index-based probing:
0→1→2→3→4 sequentially via setTemp(). Probe disconnect 
indicated by -999.9°C value.

device_families.description: Pro-grade thermometer with history and IEEE 754 float encoding
device_families.protocol_notes:
Uses IEEE 754 float32 instead of integer encoding. 
History upload: multi-segment BLE Mesh messages with 
first-chunk and continuation flags. Probe reading uses 
setTemp(0..3) flow with response-based state machine.
device_families.temperature_encoding_detail: 32-bit IEEE 754 floating point (Java float) in big-endian byte order

mesh_protocol.description:
ThermoPro uses standard BLE Mesh v1.0/1.1 with the GATT Proxy bearer.
The phone acts as a mesh provisioner, configuring the thermometer node.
Mesh PDUs contain opcodes (1-3 octets), TTL, IV index, sequence numbers,
and segmented lower transport for messages exceeding the MTU.
